title: Consciousness is the self
hookLine: a teacher dreams of words cut into a rock, and the first of them says consciousness is the self
carry: consciousness is the self, and it's shiva's own
tomorrow: how can knowing be a trap?

cards: A rock on a mountainside in Kashmir. That's where this story says a teaching was waiting. Tradition remembers a teacher named Vasugupta, a devotee of Shiva, who had a dream.
In it, Shiva told him that on a certain mountain there was a great stone, and on the stone, words were cut: short lines of teaching that had been forgotten. Vasugupta woke up.
And now he has to decide what a dream is worth.

teach.b: Tradition says Vasugupta went. He climbed to the place from the dream, found the stone and touched it, and it turned over, showing the lines carved underneath.
Some commentators tell it differently: Shiva taught him in the dream itself. Either way, the tradition treats the Shiva Sutras as given, not invented. This is the opening of Kashmir Shaivism.
A sutra is a thread, a line so short a teacher has to unpack it.
And the very first thread of this book is two words: chaitanyam atma. Consciousness is the self. Sit with how strange and how simple that is.
It doesn't say you have consciousness, the way you have a phone or a cold. It says you are it. Not the body, not the name, not the job title, not the mood you woke up in.
Those come and go. The awareness that notices them coming and going: that's the self. And Kashmir Shaivism takes one more step.
That consciousness isn't a small private light in each head.
It's Shiva's own, one consciousness, appearing as everything and everyone. So the first line of the book is also a line about God.
Hindus call the self atman; this book says the atman is awareness itself, and that awareness is Shiva.

Commentators in this tradition, like Kshemaraja, linger over these two words, and read the rest of the book as unfolding from them. The names pointed out at Shiva. This thread points in, at whoever is listening.

how: In the Kashmir Shaiva tradition the Shiva Sutras are studied with a teacher and a commentary, such as Kshemaraja's, one short line at a time.

games.q: you're Vasugupta. you dream that Shiva has hidden teaching on a stone on a mountain. you wake up. what do you do?
o: shrug it off as a dream.
climb the mountain and look for the stone.
games.why: tradition says he went, found the stone, touched it, and it turned over, showing the sutras carved underneath.

practice: Let sounds come in, a car, a fan, your own breathing, and thoughts too, and each time something appears, say softly to yourself: noticed.

Every so often, turn around and ask what is doing the noticing, and without answering in words, rest in whatever is aware for a breath or two. If you pray, you can hold the first sutra, consciousness is the self, as your line.

wordCard.voice: Kashmir Shaivism opening. A new book, the Shiva Sutras, said to be found on a rock, and its first thread: chaitanyam atma, consciousness is the self.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the first of the Shiva Sutras, consciousness (chaitanyam) is the self (atma).

carryVoice: Your line: consciousness is the self, and it's Shiva's own. Moods come and go; the awareness that notices them is the self. Back tomorrow, same hill.
